basis: Bacterial infection defines this umbrella; no single anatomical organ is consistently affected across its subtypes.
Isolated failure of sperm production and motility; reproductive dysfunction without demonstrated endocrine failure.
Intellectual disability, intestinal/oral anomalies and cardiac defects define the syndrome; damaging coloboma and microphthalmia occur in 80-99%.
Proximal tubular dysfunction with acidosis and electrolyte wasting; osteomalacia, rickets and fracture susceptibility occur in 30-79%.
Autoimmune central, autonomic and peripheral nerve dysfunction, commonly associated with CASPR2 antibodies; cramps and sweating do not establish other organ damage.
Gonococcal infection of intraocular tissues; both ocular location and infectious mechanism define the disease.
Familial neuropathy affecting the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.
Optic nerve atrophy and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; hearing impairment is only occasional, and hypotonia alone does not establish muscle damage.
Congenital joint rigidity establishes musculoskeletal involvement; no evidence supports additional organs.
Toxoplasma infection directly causes encephalitis or brain abscesses.
Definition specifies generally no intrinsic phenotype; unmasked recessive diseases are separate conditions. Discordant HPO findings do not establish organ damage from UPD itself.
Neuroendocrine tumor arising in sympathetic chromaffin paraganglia or adrenal medulla; catecholamine secretion alone does not establish additional organ damage.
Chromosomal neurodevelopmental syndrome with intellectual and speech developmental impairment; supplied additional organ abnormalities are individually occasional (5-29%).
Recurrent eyelid edema causes permanent stretching and atrophy of eyelid tissue; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and cataracts occur in 80-99%. Coarctation has conflicting 2/2 versus 5-29% annotations and is excluded.
Benign brown-fat tumor arising within the central nervous system; anatomical tumor location determines the axis.
Primary ovarian endocrine failure, with low estradiol and elevated FSH in 11/11 patients.
Male breast tissue enlargement; breast has no axis, and an underlying endocrine disorder is not established by this concept.
Glycolytic defect with hemolysis and neurodegeneration; muscle atrophy occurs in 80-99%. Immune dysfunction omitted by cap; respiratory failure is neuromuscular.
Mitochondrial defect with defining cardiomyopathy and psychomotor delay; liver injury has elevated enzymes in 4/5. Renal disease reported in one patient, omitted by cap.
Congenital bilateral obstruction of the posterior nasal airway; nasal airways belong to the pulmonary axis.
Inherited cortical movement disorder causing progressive myoclonus; involuntary muscle movements originate in the nervous system.
Congenital atrial septal defect; associated anomalous pulmonary venous return is also cardiovascular.
Inherited multiple cutaneous cylindromas, with skin and subcutaneous tumors; no common extra-cutaneous damage is established.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder causing motor pathway degeneration; amyotrophy is neurogenic. Direct mitochondrial myopathy and ocular abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
